label: GitHub Code 2025 — Python
description: Real-world GitHub Python source files (the "content" field), streamed and sampled to 5,000 documents from a 55-language, 143M-row code corpus.
highlight: A Python file embedding real HTML fooled the HTML-document detector into running trafilatura on the whole file, which confidently extracted an unrelated fragment and discarded most of the actual code. Fixed with a new --content-hint not-html flag that completely disables HTML tag stripping for known code inputs. Even the previous "lightweight" stripping mode proved unsafe, since <...> is common Python syntax (for example in Flask route parameters, chained comparisons, or generics) rather than HTML markup. Separately, the content-type heuristic correctly identifies about 99.5% of documents in this dataset as code (compared with roughly 90% on the math dataset). Nearly all remaining ghost-token matches occur in legitimate code that manipulates tokenizer special tokens—for example, checking for <|endoftext|> or mocking <bos>/<eos> tokens—rather than indicating dataset contamination. The only notable false positives are [prompt] and [cls], which come from ordinary Python identifiers (a list literal and a class-method parameter, respectively) that happen to overlap with the ghost-token vocabulary
facts: 28.9M rows (Python config); 143.7M rows across all 55 languages
Real GitHub Python source files, the "content" field
